newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: The Dutch main share index, the AEX, entirely recouped the losses it had suffered on Monday, as market players found comfort in both a higher close and start of Wall Street and a strong bond market on Tuesday.
The AEX ended at 727.84, 12.62 points above Monday's close, while the midcap's AMX added 16.10 points to close at 1086.99.
Dealers said market sentiment was good, as a widely expected 0.25 percent hike in U.S. interest rates -- likely to be announced this evening -- had already been fully priced in.
"Yet, the market did focus on it today. We're all waiting," one dealer said.
Together with ING warrants, ING shares topped the volume list in heavy arbitrage trade. ING shares ended 2.60 guilders higher at 71.80.

The other financial stocks also starred, making up for most of Monday's losses. ABN Amro added 2.20 at 126.90, FortisAmev ended up 2.60 guilders at 71.50, while Aegon closed up 1.20 at 131.00 guilders.
"It's all in the interest rates story. With hopes for a hike likely to be soon transformed into reality, fears will disappear," one dealer said.
Another said financials were boosted by a stronger guilder.
"A stronger guilder against the mark reduces the need for a hike in the special advances rate," he said.
The Dutch special advances rate currently stands at 2.90 percent, ten basis points below its German counterpart the repo.

Heineken added 12.20 guilders to 334.00, boosted by Lehman Brothers' decision to put the brewer on its European recommended list. One dealer downplayed the rise, saying trade in the stock was relatively thin.
The entire publishing sector performed well, but Elsevier stood out as market players digested the U.S. science deal announced on Monday.
"The news fell in a bad market yesterday. But analysts must have spelled out the advantages of it since," one dealer said.
Elsevier said on Monday it planned to make a $320 million public offer for MDL Information Systems Inc.
Temp agency Randstad continued its recent rally, adding 4.40 guilders to 150.90 on the announcement of a 2.5-for-one share split.
Dealers said they expected the Dutch share market to continue on a positive path as the undertone was healthy.
"The dollar, bonds, FOMC,... all point in a good direction. And there's a solid support around 700," one dealer said.
